column1: # Idiom drill. One row per idiom. The question is one of q1–q4, in English.
# avoidN lists other idioms in THIS set that could also answer that question.
# Distractors are chosen only from the rest of the set.

column3: a number too large to count
column4: We sold cakes today. I stopped counting after the first hour.
column6: She tried to thank every donor. There were too many names.
column8: Ants covered the path. You might as well not count them.
column10: The comments on his video would fill a book.

column3: people or things arriving from every direction
column4: Relatives came to the wedding from the north, the south, and overseas.
column6: When the alarm rang, people ran in from every street around the square.
column8: Questions came from classmates, from teachers, and from the parents.
column10: The smell of bread pulled customers out of all the neighboring villages.

column3: handling something that might break or spill
column4: She carried the cake across the room as if it were glass.
column6: He opened the old letter with two fingers.
column8: The nurse set the baby down without a sound.
column10: I tested every step on the frozen pond.

column3: something happens and nobody can explain it
column4: The kitchen lights turn on at midnight. Nobody touches the switch.
column6: He laughed during the quiet part of the film and could not say why.
column8: My phone sent her a message. I never typed it.
column10: A stranger bowed to me on the bus, then got off without a word.

column3: frozen, with no idea what to do next
column4: The interviewer asked three questions at once. She just stared.
column6: Both children were crying and the soup was boiling over. He stood in the doorway.
column8: They handed him the microphone with no warning. His mind went blank.
column10: The map, the tickets, and the announcement all disagreed. Nobody moved.

column3: the feeling acts before the person decides
column4: The film ended and she was crying before she noticed.
column6: He heard the old song and started singing in the supermarket.
column8: When the dog came home, the child hugged it and would not let go.
column10: I saw the score and cheered in the library.

column3: two people do the same thing without planning it
column4: We had not spoken, but we both brought soup to the same friend.
column6: The two judges wrote the same score without looking at each other.
column8: Mom and I texted "come home" at the same minute.
column10: Neither of us planned it. We both stood up to leave.

column3: two things cannot be told apart
column4: The twins wore the same coat, the same shoes, and the same haircut.
column6: I held the fake vase next to the real one and could not tell them apart.
column8: Her answers and his used the same sentences in the same order.
column10: The two apartments match: same sofa, same lamp, same view.

column3: a pair of opposites, not merely "not the same"
column4: The brothers grew up together. One saves every coin. The other spends it the same day.
column6: This coffee is bitter. The other cup is all milk and sugar.
column8: Monday the room was silent. Tuesday it was a party.
column10: Her first draft was cold and formal. The second sounds like a friend talking.

column3: a plan survives whatever goes wrong
column4: The train is cancelled and the road is closed. She is still coming tonight.
column6: He has a fever and says he will take the exam anyway.
column8: We lost the map. We are not turning back.
column10: They cut the budget. The show still opens on Friday.

column3: this is simply what ought to happen
column4: You broke it, so of course you pay for it.
column6: She is the host. Of course she greets people at the door.
column8: He borrowed the book. Everyone expects him to bring it back.
column10: Parents feed their children. Nobody treats that as a special favor.

column3: this goes beyond every earlier case
column4: The river has flooded before, but never over the bridge.
column6: The shop has had queues, but never around the block.
column8: Snow here is rare. Snow in June has not happened.
column10: He has been late. He has never missed the exam entirely.

column3: a result that is hard to believe
column4: She learned the whole piece in one afternoon. The teacher kept replaying the recording.
column6: A paper boat made it across the lake. We still do not see how.
column8: He memorized the guest list after hearing it once.
column10: The old phone turned on after ten years in a drawer.

column3: the hard part took someone almost no effort
column4: I fought with the jar for five minutes. She opened it with two fingers.
column6: The test took me an hour. He handed it in before I finished the first page.
column8: We needed a rest halfway up. The guide never slowed down.
column10: I had a dictionary open. She read the sign and answered.

column3: someone starts before it is time
column4: The cake was still hot. The children were already reaching for a slice.
column6: He saw the score online and called me before the match ended.
column8: The parcel arrived and she tore the tape in the hallway.
column10: Class is not over. His bag is already on his shoulder.

column3: an event with no warning
column4: We were mid-sentence when the alarm started.
column6: The bus braked. Nobody had seen the deer.
column8: Sunshine, then hail, in the time it took to open the umbrella.
column10: He was hired on Monday. The project was cancelled on Tuesday morning.

column3: talking with nobody else in the conversation
column4: Grandpa walks around the garden answering questions nobody asked.
column6: She repeats the shopping list out loud in the empty kitchen.
column8: He argues with himself while he fixes the bicycle.
column10: On the platform she whispered the train times, though she was not talking to me.

column3: joy you can see
column4: He came in humming and set the table early.
column6: The children saw the beach and ran ahead laughing.
column8: She got the part. She has been smiling at strangers.
column10: When the results came, the whole team talked at once, all grinning.

column3: every method is tried for one goal
column4: He called every shop in town looking for that one battery.
column6: She tried three buses, a taxi, and a friend's car to arrive before noon.
column8: They asked the neighbors, posted online, and walked the park to find the cat.
column10: I rewrote the recipe four ways so we could make it without eggs.

column3: everything else stops for this one effort
column4: For three weeks he did nothing but prepare for this match.
column6: She closed the shop, turned off her phone, and sat down with the tax forms.
column8: The kitchen stopped every other order to finish this wedding cake.
column10: He put the game away and studied until morning.
